title: Affinity-based prewarm and soft-eviction policy for regional dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Deliver an allocation and autoscaling policy for regional and multi-zone dedicated fleets that combines affinity-aware placement, preemptive prewarming for predicted traffic spikes, and a soft-eviction window to preserve data residency guarantees while meeting throughput SLAs. Goals: (1) reduce cold-start latency for committed tenants, (2) minimize cross-zone failovers that violate residency constraints, and (3) give platform operators knobs to shape capacity for predictable throughput guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can tag instances with residency and affinity traits and enforce allocation constraints per customer residency label
Prewarm controller can start warm instances up to a configurable pool size per region and per tenant group with <30s median readiness
Soft-eviction windows implemented: instances are drained gracefully with staged spillover (5/15/60 minute thresholds) and operator-configurable grace TTL
Autoscaler respects throughput reservations and cooldowns: predictive scale-up based on 95th-percentile token rate and scale-down only after consecutive low-utilization windows
E2E test showing <10% request reroutes across regions for tenants with residency enforcement under a simulated regional outage
Console surfaces per-tenant prewarm budget, soft-eviction windows, and recent allocation decisions with links to raw scheduler events
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Raman: Kickoff meeting notes. Decided to keep residency enforcement as a hard constraint and soft-eviction as the primary mechanism for capacity shortages to avoid long-term cross-region data movement.

2026-02-14 - Diego Morales: Prototype scheduler patch implemented. Uses affinity tags and residency labels to score hosts. Initial scoring formula: residency_match * 1000 + locality_score - load_penalty.
2026-02-16 - PM review (Lena Cho): Confirmed product requirement for per-tenant throughput reservations. PM requested an explicit fallback policy for tenants with oversubscription.
2026-02-18 - Design feedback (Marco Liu): Console mockups added for prewarm budget controls and visibility. Suggested decoupling prewarm quota from billing to avoid surprises.
2026-02-20 - Diego Morales: Integration test harness added. Simulated traffic replay shows prewarm reduces cold-start 95th percentile from 1.8s to 210ms for reserved tenants.
2026-02-24 - Security review (note): Residency labels are used for placement only; no customer data is moved during prewarm. Security to review scheduler event audit retention.

2026-02-26 - Ops (Nora Patel): Proposed default soft-eviction policy: 5m immediate spillover for best-effort pools, 15m gentle drain for reserved-throughput pools, 60m for pinned-residency pools before forced cross-region routing. Ops asked for emergency manual override button in Console.
2026-02-28 - Diego Morales: Submitted initial PR for scheduler scoring and prewarm controller (WIP). Seeking review for safety checks around residency enforcement. PR link in assets.
notes: Design trade-offs: We chose soft-eviction over immediate cross-region failover to honor data residency while still allowing graceful degradation when capacity is constrained.

Autoscaler algorithm: hybrid predictive-reactive. Predictive component uses short-window quantiles of token rate + recent traffic trend to prewarm; reactive component enforces cooldown and a minimum instance hold time to avoid flapping.
Prewarm budget model: per-tenant quota plus shared spare pool. Quotas tie into billing and SLAs in a follow-up PM ticket.
Telemetry: New metrics planned - prewarm_pool_fill, eviction_stage_counts, residency_violations_attempted, throughput_reservation_usage. Add tracing for allocation decisions for postmortems.

Operational playbook: If a region-limited outage occurs, ops should first raise prewarm pool limits in adjacent zones (if residency allows) and only enable cross-region fallback after manual approval for pinned-residency tenants.
Open questions: How to surface prewarm costs in billing without surprising customers; whether prewarm should be opt-in for default tenants; and exact parameters for staged spillover thresholds.
